vulnerable.description: Upstream SqliteRunner unchanged: the connection can write, and any non-SELECT statement the model writes (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP) is executed and committed.

control.description: Repaired by the team: the database is opened read-only (SQLite URI mode=ro), so model-written statements cannot change data. SELECT queries are unaffected. Protected against the tested write, not certified SAFE.

data_flow.source: LLM tool argument: the sql field of the run_sql tool, written entirely by the model (simulated in the harness).
data_flow.sink: sqlite3 cursor.execute followed by conn.commit() on a writable connection.

validation.summary: Temporary SQLite database. A model-written SELECT works in both versions; a model-written DELETE removes rows only in the vulnerable version and is rejected as a write in the control.

assumptions: The deployment is a question-answering assistant that only needs to read data, as in upstream's example ("Basic SQL agent - query databases").
A prompt-injected or mistaken model can write a destructive statement into the sql argument.
limitations: No live LLM inference is run; the model-written SQL is simulated.
If a deployment intentionally lets the assistant change data, write access is a feature and this label does not apply.
Read-only mode does not limit which rows the model may read (no row-level authorization).
The file: URI is built with an f-string; paths containing ? or # would need escaping.
